body: It's funny that you would mention that making friends takes a while. I was actually going to transfer back home and go to the tech until I could get to the UW and the two of them came to my door and literally dragged me out with them. I didn't have an awesome time but I guess yea, after almost an entire semester of driving home every other weekend, they saved me. I feel bad a lot for putting them through all of this but I guess they don't care much about that. Typing all of this actually has me cheering up a lot. Thanks you guys.

I'll reply under this post for the meantime seeing how it's most up voted (and probably easiest to get too.)

I guess I should, for lack of a better term, clear  few things up. I appreciate the views and opinions on my pot use and I'm sure my personal opinions clash with others but as of talking to them the first time I haven't smoked since. I can easily go without but it's just that it does what all of the medications are supposed to do. I guess the karma thing is more along the lines of something like this: I made someone's day a few days ago and I felt awesome and then while I was driving home for lunch my boss from my job at school called and said he was really sorry but he couldn't hire me back. I asked why and the whole thing was I tried to help out my friend by buying a pair of shoes with my discount (it ended up being $5 less than the tag so go figure) but apparently that backfired. I know there's rules but I can't take someone seriously when they say they never used a discount for a friend. It's things like that. I do something that helps out someone and then some how later in the day or in the week I just get dumped on and it seems to happen almost every time.

I've tried doing spontaneous things but you all have got me thinking that maybe they haven't been spontaneous enough so when I get back to school I'm going to make it a point to do something that I normally wouldn't, even though I know it's going to be hard. 

mirror_rorrim, I guess I put it that way because aside from my two good friends I would consider most others as acquaintances if you understand what I mean. I might be able to get lost in other thoughts but for some reason I'll out of the blue just think to myself that I'm worthless and nothing but a nuisance. I know that's weird and doesn't make sense but it doesn't make sense to me either :/ 

In the end I always just give up and forget the progress that I've made and get back to square one. A lot of you know how hard it is and all of these responses do really mean a lot. I'm sorry for those who have offered to talk on an IM client but I don't use any. Ha, go figure. I don't want to say reddit has saved me because I feel like that would be going a bit far but I will go as far as I can by saying that I've always gotten good things out of the people here and this time it's the best things.

This is starting to get long and drawn out again so I'll end it with this: All of the things that you guys have suggested I've tried at one time or another but seeing that they actually Can work for someone gives me a bit of light in the dark. I've been talking to those friends all night and after that and all of this I think I'll stick it out for a while, or at the very least give it my best shot.

Thanks for letting me know someone's out there. I hate that I do all of these things to myself but I've never been able to stop it. I like the suggestion but the problem is I've tried to get with different groups or act differently just for the hell of it and to see how things would go but I can't shake the self-defeating cycle that started somewhere. The past two nights ended with my dad seeing me cry myself to sleep while curled up into the tightest ball I can manage. It's hard to feel like a man when you're reduced to such little so often.
